finalText:
Two usual reasons.

**New objects and functions each render.** If you write `{()=> doThing()}` or `{{color: 'red'}}` right inside the parent's render, React sees a brand new function or object every time, even though it looks the same. The child then gets a "different" prop.

**No memo on the child.** By default, a child re-renders whenever its parent does, no matter what props it gets. Wrapping it in `React.memo(Child)` makes React skip the re-render when props are truly unchanged.

To fix it: wrap the child in `React.memo`, and wrap any functions or objects you pass down in `useCallback` or `useMemo` so they keep the same identity between renders. If you'd like, paste the component and I can point at the exact line causing it.
